name: Kingdom of Dahomey
notes: Houegbadja/Wegbaja (r. c.1645-1685) most consistently credited as effective first king (built Abomey palaces, formalized Annual Customs, centralized religious authority). Do-Aklin (c.1600-1620) and Dakodonou (c.1620-1645) precede him in the dynastic king-list, but Robin Law's source-critical historiography argues Dakodonou may have been retroactively inserted in the 18th century to legitimize the dynasty's claim over the Abomey plateau's original inhabitants — flag the earliest portion of the king-list as contested, not settled. Absorbed into French West Africa after the Second Franco-Dahomean War (1892-94), King Béhanzin captured 1893.
